analysis_sections.text: The reconstruction keeps the broad head and facial layout recognizable, but replaces much of the original fine appearance with a banded, tiled structure. It offers a different view of the same studio face for comparison with the source crop. The display illustrates graph filtering; claims about specific frequency abnormalities would require additional evidence beyond the reconstruction itself.
analysis_sections.title: A transformed view of the same face

analysis_sections.text: The middle displayed pair places its strongest positive readout in the lower central grid, with other positive cells extending beyond the attention selection. The signed values tell us which saved patch features support the manipulated direction at the classifier readout. They do not identify a particular facial defect or production process. Comparing pairs reveals how the distribution of that support changes with the sampled expression.
analysis_sections.title: Where the classifier readout supports its decision

analysis_sections.text: The learned attention map emphasizes a compact central facial region, spanning a different area from the strongest lower-grid contribution. The explanation head is trained separately on frozen detector features to propose important patches. Its unsigned scores describe that proposal, not a probability of manipulation or the detector’s internal feature-extraction weights. The connected selection makes this learned focus easy to inspect on the original face.
analysis_sections.title: The explanation head’s proposed focus

analysis_sections.text: Some whole-curve comparisons favor the selected central region and others favor the matched controls. The recorded evidence therefore supports discussing a measured regional response, while keeping the proposal distinct from a fully qualified local explanation. The video-level classification remains strong. Hiding and restoring a proposal tests model reliance on those input patches; it does not identify the editing method or establish a unique cause.
analysis_sections.title: What the selected-region measurements establish

report.conclusion: The detector’s output favors manipulated; no visual cues were observed in the original footage.

diagnosis.evidence_synthesis: The first pass detected no visible artifacts. SSTGNN’s calibrated fake score exceeds the strong classification threshold. Regional experiments show mixed support but do not alter the video-level decision. Attention and contribution maps highlight central facial patches, consistent with the model’s internal response.

inherited_editor_changes.after:
A bald man wearing a dark suit and shirt sits in a talk-show studio with a cityscape backdrop. In one short sequence he lowers both raised hands; later he turns his head and changes expression while his hands are below the frame. The face remains prominent enough to compare the original scene with the saved spectral and heatmap views.

SSTGNN strongly favors manipulated. Signed contributions extend through central and lower grid locations, while the learned attention region is more compact and central. This difference is useful: one map describes directional classifier support and the other proposes a connected focus for inspection. Recorded regional comparisons give mixed support.
inherited_editor_changes.before: The video shows a bald man in a dark suit seated in a studio setting, gesturing with both hands raised while speaking. His expression shifts subtly across frames, with consistent lighting and background architecture visible behind him. The detector delivers a decisive fake classification with high calibrated confidence, driven primarily by spectral and spatial features in the central facial region. Signed contribution maps highlight strong positive evidence around the nose and upper lip, while unsigned attention converges tightly on the mid-face, reinforcing where the model concentrates its decision logic.

inherited_editor_changes.before: The classifier’s decision is robust and unambiguous, with spectral and spatial branches contributing most of the positive signal. Regional intervention tests yield mixed results: half the curve comparisons favor the selected area, but no intervention passes all verification checks, indicating the region explains part—but not all—of the detector’s confidence.

inherited_editor_changes.before: The selected central face region yields mixed support in intervention tests: four of eight whole-curve comparisons favor it, and endpoint effects vary by operation and control type. Still, the region remains the best available explanation for the classifier’s focus, even if not definitively causal.
